The heat and movement of the voyage were found to improve the wine dramatically, and it sold at high prices. Estufagem and canteiro methods were developed to reproduce the effect on land.

A Spanish category for single estates with a distinctive terroir and reputation, created in 2003. Each pago is its own appellation and must make wine from its own vineyards. There are a couple of dozen, mostly in Castilla-La Mancha, Navarra and Valencia, the first being Dominio de Valdepusa (Marqués de Griñón) in 2003. It allows top estates to stand outside regional DOs, though not all pagos have international reputations.

Port from a single exceptional year, 'declared' by a house about three times a decade, after about two years in wood and with the approval of the IVDP. It is bottled unfiltered and ages for decades in bottle, throwing a heavy sediment. Famous declared years include 1945, 1963, 1977, 1994, 2011, 2016 and 2017. Single-quinta vintage Ports are made in undeclared years.

The film of yeast that grows on the surface of Savagnin in partly filled barrels in the Jura, similar to sherry's flor but in a cooler, drier climate. It protects the wine from oxidation while yeasts consume some alcohol and produce sotolon and acetaldehyde, which give vin jaune its walnut and curry aromas. Wines aged under voile but not long enough to be vin jaune are often labelled 'sous voile' or 'tradition'.

Soils derived from volcanic rocks and ash: basalt, andesite, tuff, pumice, scoria (picón) and lava. They range from fertile to barren and are often rich in minerals and well drained. Famous examples include Etna, Santorini, Vesuvius, Campi Flegrei, Lanzarote, Tenerife, Tokaj, Soave, Kaiserstuhl and parts of Chile and Armenia. Sandy volcanic soils often keep phylloxera away, so ungrafted vines survive.

Vintners Quality Alliance, the appellation and quality system in Ontario (law since 1999) and British Columbia. VQA wines must be made entirely from grapes grown in the province's designated viticultural areas and pass a tasting panel. VQA also regulates icewine. Wines blended from imported and Canadian grapes, once labelled 'Cellared in Canada', are now called 'International Canadian Blends' and cannot carry VQA.

Fermenting red grapes with some or all bunches left intact, stems included, rather than destemmed. It adds freshness, spice, floral aromas and a firmer tannic structure, and can lower alcohol slightly because stems absorb some. Burgundy producers such as Domaine Dujac and Domaine de la Romanée-Conti are known for high whole-cluster percentages, and the technique is common in Pinot Noir, Syrah and Gamay. Unripe stems can give green, bitter flavours.

A soil series in Oregon's Willamette Valley formed from uplifted ancient marine sediments (sandstone and siltstone). Brown and well drained, it is found in the Yamhill-Carlton and Ribbon Ridge AVAs. Pinot Noir from Willakenzie is often described as darker-fruited and more tannic than from volcanic Jory soils, a contrast Oregon growers often taste side by side.

South Africa's appellation system, introduced in 1973, dividing the country into geographical units, regions, districts and wards, such as the Stellenbosch district and its Simonsberg-Stellenbosch ward. A WO wine must be 100 percent from the stated area. The system certifies origin, vintage and variety and includes 'estate wine' rules. Certification seals appear on bottles.

A climate classification devised by Albert Winkler and Maynard Amerine at UC Davis in 1944, based on growing degree days: the sum of daily mean temperatures above 10 degrees Celsius (50 degrees Fahrenheit) from April to October. It divides regions into five classes, from Region I (cool, under 1,390 degree days Celsius, such as Champagne or the Mosel) to Region V (very hot, such as California's Central Valley). It is simple and widely used.

A group of porous aluminium silicate minerals formed from volcanic ash, able to hold water and exchange minerals. Tokaj's volcanic hills contain zeolite, along with rhyolite, andesite and clays such as nyirok, which some producers credit for the wines' minerality and freshness. Zeolite was even mined near Tokaj. Its high water retention helps vines in dry summers.
